theme: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
queries_run: gh search repos polymarket api python --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos kalshi api data --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos manifold markets dataset --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos "prediction market" historical dataset --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos manifold-markets api client --limit 30 --sort stars
gh search repos kalshi historical data csv --limit 30 --sort updated

candidates.name: polymarket-historical-data (manja316)
candidates.what_it_holds: Claims 13,964 Polymarket markets, 10.8M price records, $11.7B+ volume as a historical price/volume archive; description does not confirm file format (likely CSV/SQLite) or whether earnings/travel/regulation category markets are tagged separately — needs a directory listing to confirm real committed files vs. a thin wrapper.
candidates.why_useful: A broad Polymarket price history would let us pull any historical ABNB-earnings-move or travel/regulation-event contracts (e.g. FIFA World Cup timing, Fed/CPI prints, government shutdown, tourism-tax votes) as point-in-time implied-probability series — relevant to gap 4 (point-in-time vintages) and gap 11/12 (events, regulation).
candidates.size_hint: 10.8M rows across 13,964 markets (per README claim, unverified)
candidates.geography: global (crypto-native prediction market, mostly US/global political and sports events)

candidates.name: polymarket-historical-data (LuciferForge)
candidates.what_it_holds: 18.6M price snapshots across 22,410 markets at 15-min resolution over a 92-day window (Mar-Jun 2026), distributed as SQLite; free sample plus a paid/full dataset link.
candidates.why_useful: High-frequency, multi-market Polymarket snapshot archive covering spring 2026 — could contain any ABNB-earnings or macro/regulation contracts active in that window; MIT licensed sample is directly pullable without scraping.

candidates.name: awesome-prediction-market-apis
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated directory of prediction-market APIs, SDKs, MCP servers, and pointers to historical order-book data sources across Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, Limitless and others; itself an awesome-list (markdown), not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Fastest way to find which of the many prediction-market API wrappers actually expose historical order-book/price series usable for point-in-time event-probability construction (gap 4, 11, 12) without re-discovering them one by one.

candidates.name: awesome-prediction-markets
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list of prediction-market analytics tools, APIs, trading bots, dashboards, arbitrage tools and data feeds covering Polymarket, Kalshi, Hyperliquid, Limitless.
candidates.why_useful: Secondary discovery list; overlaps with Ong-pogs's list but CC0-licensed, useful cross-check for acquisition methods on event/earnings contracts.

candidates.name: PyManifold
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the Manifold Markets public API (18 stars, actively maintained through Jan 2026); wraps market listing, bet history, and price/probability history endpoints — Manifold's API is free/keyless for reads.
candidates.why_useful: Manifold hosts many community-made questions on company earnings beats, travel/tourism events, and regulatory outcomes; this client is a one-command way to pull full probability history (with timestamps) for any such market — directly serves the point-in-time vintage gap (4) for event-probability nowcasts around the Nov 5 print or regulatory votes (gap 12).
candidates.size_hint: small client library, no bundled data
candidates.time_coverage: pulls live/historical via API, Manifold history back to 2022

candidates.name: prediction_markets (futuur)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit unifying Futuur, Manifold Markets, and Polymarket APIs for searching, correlating, and trading; includes market-matching logic across the three platforms by title similarity.
candidates.why_useful: Cross-platform market matching would let us assemble a merged event-probability panel (earnings, travel, regulation questions) across three sources rather than one, improving coverage for point-in-time series (gap 4).

candidates.name: predmarket
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library 'predmarket' unifying Kalshi and Polymarket API access into one interface for market/price retrieval.
candidates.why_useful: Lower-friction acquisition method if we want to pull Kalshi's regulated CFTC event contracts (economic/regulatory, e.g. Fed decisions, government actions) alongside Polymarket without writing two separate clients.

candidates.name: kalshi-price-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Advertises Kalshi historical data and a price API: live yes/no prices, full order-book depth, WebSocket streaming, and a Python client (DepthFeed) — appears to be a hosted product with a thin open client rather than committed historical files; needs directory listing to confirm any bundled data vs. pure API wrapper.
candidates.why_useful: Kalshi is CFTC-regulated and carries economic-data and event contracts (e.g. CPI, Fed, government shutdown, possibly travel/tourism-adjacent) that are more likely to be well-formed probability series than crypto-native Polymarket; order-book depth would give more than just last price.
candidates.size_hint: unclear, likely hosted service not bundled files

candidates.name: kalshi-dune-community-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Script that fetches Kalshi market data via API and stores it into a public Dune Analytics table (community dataset), rather than committing files to the repo.
candidates.why_useful: If the Dune table is public and queryable, it could serve as a continuously-updated free Kalshi archive without needing to run the scraper ourselves — worth checking the Dune table directly (external host).

candidates.name: prediction_markets (kyleyhw)
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts analyzing Polymarket/Kalshi market microstructure (bid-ask spreads, arbitrage detection) and explicitly verifying historical data integrity via CLOB and Gamma APIs.
candidates.why_useful: The data-integrity verification code is a useful template for point-in-time correctness checks (rule 2 of our own project) when pulling prediction-market vintages, even though the repo itself stores no dataset.

candidates.name: Futuur-Kalshi-Polymarket-API-data-Automation
candidates.what_it_holds: Client-commissioned project retrieving ongoing-event data from Futuur, Kalshi, and Polymarket APIs and matching equivalent markets across platforms by title.
candidates.why_useful: Same cross-platform matching value as futuur/prediction_markets; a second independent implementation to sanity-check the matching approach if we ever build an event-probability panel.

candidates.name: prediction-markets-skill
candidates.what_it_holds: A 'Claude skill' packaging read-only Kalshi + Polymarket market-data retrieval with zero dependencies and no API keys required, meant to stop AI agents from hallucinating prediction-market API calls.
candidates.why_useful: Directly reusable as a no-key, no-dependency method for our own agents to pull live Kalshi/Polymarket prices on any ABNB-earnings, FIFA World Cup, or regulation-outcome market if we decide to build a live panel.

candidates.name: manifold_prediction
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as 'research, datasets, evaluation tooling, and trained baselines for Manifold prediction-market quality and engagement' — unclear from description alone whether real market-outcome data is committed or this is a quality/engagement-scoring research repo; would need a contents listing to confirm.
candidates.why_useful: If it holds Manifold market outcome/calibration data, it could support point-in-time calibration checks for any Manifold-hosted ABNB or travel-event questions we later use.

candidates.name: polymarket-tennis
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT, observe-only toolkit that discovers Polymarket sports markets via the Gamma API and matches them to live match data to watch market price vs. live score/server/break-point in real time.
candidates.why_useful: Not travel/ABNB-relevant directly, but it is the most-starred (317) worked example of pattern-matching a specific event-market category on Polymarket's Gamma API by topic — a reusable template if we later want to isolate ABNB-earnings or World-Cup-timing markets the same way.

candidates.name: sports-skills
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source agent skills (SKILL.md format) for live sports data and prediction markets covering football, F1, Kalshi, and Polymarket, with zero API keys required.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal for ABNB directly (sports-focused), but demonstrates a no-key pattern for pulling Kalshi/Polymarket data that could be adapted to non-sports event categories (regulation, macro) relevant to gap 11/12.

candidates.name: kalshi (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent third-party documentation profile of Kalshi's public REST/WebSocket API surface (endpoints, auth, market/order/position data availability) rather than any data or client code.
candidates.why_useful: Useful as an API-surface reference to scope what event categories (economics, weather, sports — regulation/travel not confirmed) Kalshi actually exposes before investing in a puller.

candidates.name: prediction-market-arbitrage
candidates.what_it_holds: Analyzes Kalshi, Polymarket, and PredictIt via API pulls plus ML-based text matching to find cross-platform market-title equivalents and mispricings; reports a backtested 9.41% mean ROI over 75 matched opportunities (Jul-Aug 2025).
candidates.why_useful: Brings PredictIt into the cross-platform matching picture (a third, older prediction-market venue with historically more political/regulatory questions), and the title-matching ML code is reusable for finding any ABNB- or travel-adjacent contract across all three venues.

notes: Search surface here is heavily saturated with single-purpose trading/arbitrage bots (dozens of near-identical 'polymarket + kalshi arbitrage bot' repos with 0-2 stars) that hold no committed data and were excluded. No repo found that stores a dataset specifically tagged to Airbnb earnings, travel demand, or STR-regulation prediction-market questions -- these platforms' event catalogs skew toward politics, crypto, sports, and macro (Fed/CPI/elections); an ABNB-specific or travel-specific market history would have to be filtered out of a general price-history dump (e.g. manja316 or LuciferForge's archives) rather than found pre-filtered. Kalshi's own historical-data-as-csv export tooling search returned zero repos, suggesting most Kalshi historical pulls live behind their own site/paid API rather than GitHub. Two curated 'awesome' lists (Ong-pogs, Marcussy34) are the fastest route to discovering further, newer tools as this space is moving fast (most repos updated within the last week of Sep 2026). Did not verify directory contents (no `gh api` calls used) given the described-but-unconfirmed nature of most of these repos; a follow-up scout with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents` budget could confirm which of manja316/LuciferForge/cherry8177's repos actually have committed data files vs. just a README claim.
